name: Execute and record
what: Implement approved nodes test-first in topological order and preserve an audit trail.
why: Implementation must remain tied to reviewed intent and verifiable evidence as the project changes.
expected_result: Only ready nodes execute; failed checks enter debugging; exact code ranges and semantic changes remain traceable.

implementation.how: Use lifecycle gates, active-node tracking, blocking write and stop hooks, semantic log events, and current red/green verification checks.
implementation.why_this_way: Deterministic gates handle facts while the skill handles human judgment and review pauses.

local_findings: Codex Companion's tested hook parser observes apply_patch paths and rejects writes outside approved scope.
external_findings: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks documents plugin-bundled PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, and PLUGIN_ROOT.
research.reuse_decision: Reuse Codex's native plugin hook lifecycle and Python's standard library; do not add a daemon.

weekly_plan.outcome: Lifecycle transitions reject unapproved or unverified work.
Blocking gates plus touched-file and semantic audit events trace completed and failed attempts.

verification.plan: Attempt invalid transitions, missing evidence, and unfinished prerequisites; each must fail before a valid node can complete.

future_use: Every later feature can inherit the same approval, execution, debugging, and recording discipline.
